tasks.title: Hybrid — piecewise force, log hit, and a false constant-rate shortcut
tasks.context: A fund starts at $A=1000$, grows at continuous force $\alpha=0.05$ until $t=\tau$ with $\alpha\tau=\ln 2$, then at force $\beta=0.025$. The target level is $M=4A$. The figure shows the piecewise path. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The target is reached strictly after the rate switch.
The hitting time equals $\ln(M/A)/\alpha$ (ignoring the switch).
The late force $\beta$ is strictly larger than the early force $\alpha$.
At the switch the fund already meets or exceeds the target $M$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Chain the segments and solve $f(t)=M$ in the late regime.

$$f(\tau)=A e^{\alpha\tau}=2A$$

$$t_{\mathrm{hit}}=\tau+\frac{\ln(M/f(\tau))}{\beta}=\tau+\frac{\ln 2}{\beta}\approx41.5888$$

$$41.5888>\tau\approx13.8629$$

The hit is strictly after the switch.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Average force is the total log-increment per unit time.

$$\bar k=\frac{\alpha\tau+\beta(t_{\mathrm{hit}}-\tau)}{t_{\mathrm{hit}}}\approx0.033333$$

$$A e^{\bar k\,t_{\mathrm{hit}}}\approx4000$$

The average force recovers the target exactly.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → False

A constant-$\alpha$ formula pretends the switch never happened.

$$t_{\alpha}=\frac{\ln(M/A)}{\alpha}=\frac{\ln 4}{\alpha}\approx27.7259$$

$$t_{\mathrm{hit}}\approx41.5888\neq27.7259$$

The no-switch formula is not the piecewise hitting time.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → False

Compare the two force parameters directly.

$$\beta=0.025,\qquad \alpha=0.05$$

$$0.025<0.05$$

The late force is smaller, not larger.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → False

Evaluate the level at the kink.

$$f(\tau)=2A=2000,\qquad M=4A=4000$$

$$2A<4A$$

At the switch the fund is still strictly below the target.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: With $\alpha\tau=\ln 2$, $f(\tau)=2A$. Target $M=4A$ forces $t_{\mathrm{hit}}=\tau+\ln 2/\beta\approx41.5888$, path-average $\bar k\approx0.033333$. Constant-$\alpha$ mis-hit $t_{\alpha}=\ln 4/\alpha\approx27.7259$.

tasks.title: Graph — crossing populations and the log meeting clock
tasks.context: Two populations follow $A(t)=A_0 e^{k_A t}$ and $B(t)=B_0 e^{k_B t}$ with $A_0=1000$, $k_A=0.03$, $B_0=1500$, $k_B=0.01$. The figure shows both paths on $[0,40]$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The populations meet at some strictly positive time before $t=40$.
The continuous force of $A$ exceeds that of $B$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Set $A_0 e^{k_A t}=B_0 e^{k_B t}$ and take logs.

$$t^*=\frac{\ln(B_0/A_0)}{k_A-k_B}\approx20.2733$$

$$0<20.2733<40$$

A unique crossing sits inside the open interval.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Evaluate both levels at the horizon.

$$A(40)\approx3320.1169,\qquad B(40)\approx2237.737$$

Population $A$ is strictly larger at the horizon.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Compare forces directly.

$$k_A=0.03>0.01=k_B$$

Force $A$ dominates force $B$.

So the statement is True.

**D.** → False

The correct log ratio is $B_0/A_0$, not $A_0/B_0$.

$$\frac{\ln(A_0/B_0)}{k_A-k_B}\approx-20.2733$$

$$t^*\approx20.2733$$

Flipping the ratio flips the sign of the meeting time.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → False

Log-growth equals force times horizon.

$$k_A\cdot40=1.2,\qquad k_B\cdot40=0.4$$

The log-increments differ because the forces differ.

So the statement is False.

tasks.title: Table — recover continuous force, then log comparisons
tasks.context: A continuous exponential path $y(t)=y_0 e^{kt}$ is observed at two times (table). Recover the force by logarithm, then judge the claims. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The doubling time is strictly less than $20$ years.
Ten years after $t=2$, the level exceeds twice $y(2)$.
The recovered force is strictly larger than $0.06$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Start from $y_2=y_1 e^{k\Delta t}$ and solve for $k$.

$$k=\frac{\ln(y_2/y_1)}{\Delta t}=\frac{\ln(y(7)/y(2))}{5}$$

$$k\approx0.05$$

The log-ratio formula is exactly the recovered force.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Doubling solves $e^{kt}=2$.

$$t_{\times 2}=\frac{\ln 2}{k}\approx13.8629$$

$$13.8629<20$$

Doubling finishes before twenty years.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Propagate ten years from the first observation.

$$y(t_1+10)=y_1 e^{10k}\approx1318.977$$

$$2y_1=1600$$

The ten-year level exceeds twice the first observation.

So the statement is True.

**D.** → True

Evaluate the log-ratio between the tabulated points.

$$\ln(y_2/y_1)=k\cdot\Delta t\approx0.25$$

$$0.25>0.2$$

The log-ratio clears the $0.2$ threshold.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → False

Compare the recovered force with $0.06$.

$$k\approx0.05\le 0.06$$

The force equals $0.05$, which is not strictly above $0.06$.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: From the table, $k=\ln(y_2/y_1)/\Delta t\approx0.05$. Doubling $t_{\times 2}\approx13.8629$; ten years after $t_1$: $y\approx1318.977$.

tasks.title: Symbolic — inverse log clock beside an exponential stock
tasks.context: A stock follows $f(t)=P e^{kt}$ with parameters $P=200>0$ and $k=0.04>0$. Let $g$ denote the inverse of $f$ as a map $\mathbb{R}\to(0,\infty)$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The natural domain of $g$ is the positive half-line $(0,\infty)$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Solve $y=P e^{kt}$ for $t$.

$$\frac{y}{P}=e^{kt}$$

$$t=\frac{1}{k}\ln(y/P)$$

That formula is exactly $g(y)$.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Compose $g$ after $f$.

$$g(f(t))=\frac{1}{k}\ln(P e^{kt}/P)=\frac{1}{k}\cdot kt=t$$

Left inverse identity holds for all real $t$.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Range of $f$ is $(0,\infty)$ because $e^{kt}>0$ always.

An inverse is defined precisely on that range.

The domain of $g$ is $(0,\infty)$.

So the statement is True.

**D.** → True

Compose $f$ after $g$ on $y>0$.

$$f(g(y))=P\exp\bigl(\ln(y/P)\bigr)=y$$

Right inverse identity holds on the positive half-line.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

Differentiate $g(y)=k^{-1}(\ln y-\ln P)$.

$$g'(y)=\frac{1}{k}\cdot\frac{1}{y}=\frac{1}{ky}$$

The logarithmic derivative matches the claim.

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Growth $f(t)=P e^{kt}$ with $P=200$, $k=0.04>0$ is bijective $\mathbb{R}\to(0,\infty)$. Inverse $g(y)=\frac{1}{k}\ln(y/P)$ satisfies $g\circ f=\mathrm{id}$ and $f\circ g=\mathrm{id}_{(0,\infty)}$.

tasks.title: Parametric — nested logs pinning an exponential stock
tasks.context: A stock $N(t)=A e^{kt}$ has unknown $A>1$ and $k>0$ constrained by the nested-log conditions $\ln(\ln A)=0$ and $\ln k=-\ln 2$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Unwind the outer logarithm.

$$\ln(\ln A)=0\implies \ln A=1\implies A=e$$

The nested constraint pins $A=e$.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Unwind the force constraint.

$$\ln k=-\ln 2\implies k=e^{-\ln 2}=\tfrac12$$

$$k=\tfrac12\neq 2$$

The force is one half, not two.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

Doubling time is $\ln 2/k$.

$$t_{\times 2}=\frac{\ln 2}{1/2}=2\ln 2\approx1.3863$$

$$2\ln 2\neq\ln 2$$

Doubling time is $2\ln 2$, not $\ln 2$.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → False

Evaluate at $t=2$.

$$N(2)=A e^{2k}=e\cdot e^{2\cdot(1/2)}=e\cdot e=e^{2}$$

$$e^{2}\neq A=e$$

After two years the stock is $e^{2}$, not $A$.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → False

Add the two constrained logs.

$$\ln(\ln A)+\ln k=0+(-\ln 2)=-\ln 2\neq 0$$

The sum equals $-\ln 2$, not zero.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Constraints $\ln(\ln A)=0$ and $\ln k=-\ln 2$ force $A=e$ and $k=1/2$. Then $t_{\times 2}=\ln 2/k=2\ln 2\approx1.3863$, and $N(2)=A e^{2k}=e^2$.

tasks.title: Piecewise — log hit before the kink, with a decaying tail
tasks.context: A level starts at $P_0=500$, grows at force $k_1=0.06$ on $[0,T]$ with $T=3$, then decays at force $k_2=-0.02$. A threshold $M=547.0871$ is watched. The figure shows the kink. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The threshold $M$ is crossed at some time strictly before $t=3$.
Because $k_2<0$, the path eventually falls back below $M$ after the switch.
The late force $k_2$ is strictly positive.
The threshold $M$ exceeds the switch level $f(3)$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Solve in the early regime $P_0 e^{k_1 t}=M$.

$$t_{\mathrm{hit}}=\frac{\ln(M/P_0)}{k_1}\approx1.5$$

$$0<1.5<3$$

The first crossing is before the kink.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

After the switch the level is $f(T)e^{k_2(t-T)}$ with $k_2<0$.

As $t\to\infty$ this tends to $0$, which lies below $M$.

By continuity it must cross $M$ again while falling.

The decaying tail re-crosses $M$ from above.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → False

Read the late force from the stem.

$$k_2=-0.02<0$$

The late force is negative, not positive.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → True

Only the early force has acted by the switch.

$$\ln(f(T)/P_0)=k_1 T=0.18$$

The log-increment at the kink is exactly $k_1 T$.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → False

Compare threshold and switch level.

$$M=547.0871,\qquad f(T)\approx598.6087$$

$$M<f(T)$$

The threshold lies strictly below the switch level.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Early force $k_1=0.06$ until $T=3$, then $k_2=-0.02<0$. $f(T)\approx598.6087$. Target $M=547.0871$ is hit at $t=\ln(M/P_0)/k_1\approx1.5\in(0,T)$.

tasks.title: Nested — log constraints on an exponential hitting clock
tasks.context: A balance $P(t)=P_0 e^{kt}$ has $P_0>1$ and $k>0$ fixed by $\ln P_0=3$ and $\ln k=-2$. The target is one $e$-fold above $P_0$, namely $M=e\cdot P_0$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Exponentiate $\ln P_0=3$.

$$P_0=e^{3}$$

The level parameter is $e^{3}$.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Exponentiate $\ln k=-2$.

$$k=e^{-2}$$

The force is $e^{-2}$.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → False

Hitting one $e$-fold solves $e^{kt}=e$, so $t=1/k$.

$$t=e^{2}\approx7.3891\neq e^{-2}$$

The hitting time is $e^{2}$, not $e^{-2}$.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → False

By construction $M/P_0=e$, so the log-ratio is $1$.

$$\ln(M/P_0)=1,\qquad k=e^{-2}$$

$$1\neq e^{-2}$$

The log-ratio is $1$, not equal to $k$.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → False

The equivalent discrete base is $e^{k}=e^{e^{-2}}$, not $e^{2}$.

$$e^{k}=e^{e^{-2}}\neq e^{2}$$

The base is far smaller than $e^{2}$.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Constraints $\ln P_0=3$ and $\ln k=-2$ give $P_0=e^3$, $k=e^{-2}$. One $e$-fold needs $t=1/k=e^2\approx7.3891$.

tasks.title: Text-dense — five entangled exp/log micro-traps
tasks.context: Fix a nominal rate $r=0.05$ and horizon $t=10$. Separately, prices drift at force $g=0.03$ while demand has constant elasticity magnitude $b=1.2$, so $\ln Q=C-b\ln P$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The absolute size of that quantity force exceeds $0.05$.
At horizon $t=10$, annual compounding $(1+r)^{t}$ stays strictly below continuous $e^{rt}$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The exponential series $e^{r}=1+r+r^{2}/2+\cdots$ exceeds $1+r$ for $r>0$.

$$e^{0.05}\approx1.051271>1+0.05$$

Continuous one-year growth beats the linear nominal.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Strict concavity of $\ln$ at $1$ gives $\ln(1+r)<r$ for $r>0$.

$$\ln(1+0.05)\approx0.04879<0.05$$

The log-linearisation overstates the log-return.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Differentiate $\ln Q=C-b\ln P$ in time.

$$\frac{d\ln Q}{dt}=-b\frac{d\ln P}{dt}=-bg$$

$$=-1.2\cdot0.03=-0.036$$

Quantity force is exactly $-bg$.

So the statement is True.

**D.** → False

Compare $|-bg|$ with $0.05$.

$$|-0.036|=0.036\le 0.05$$

The absolute force is $0.036$, not above $0.05$.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → True

Because $1+r<e^{r}$, raising both sides to power $t>0$ preserves the inequality.

$$(1+r)^{t}\approx1.6289,\qquad e^{rt}\approx1.6487$$

Annual compounding trails continuous compounding.

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Micro-facts: $e^{r}>1+r$ and $\ln(1+r)<r$ for $r=0.05$; quantity force $-bg=-0.036$; discrete $(1+r)^10.0<e^{rt}$ at $t=10$.

tasks.title: Rebuild — force from two observations, then multiple hitting clocks
tasks.context: Only two observations of a continuous exponential stock are known (table): $y(0)=1200$ and $y(6)\approx1436.66$. Rebuild the force, then compare doubling and tripling clocks. The figure is the semi-log view. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Doubling time is strictly less than $25$ years.
Tripling time is strictly larger than doubling time.
At the doubling time the level is exactly twice $y(0)$.
On a semi-log plot of $\ln y$ against $t$, the slope equals the rebuilt force.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Two-point log recovery.

$$k=\frac{\ln(y_1/y_0)}{t_1}\approx0.03$$

That quotient is the rebuilt continuous force.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Doubling clock.

$$T_{\times 2}=\frac{\ln 2}{k}\approx23.1049$$

$$23.1049<25$$

Doubling finishes before twenty-five years.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Because $\ln 3>\ln 2$ and $k>0$, tripling takes longer.

$$T_{\times 3}=\frac{\ln 3}{k}\approx36.6204>23.1049$$

Tripling strictly follows doubling.

So the statement is True.

**D.** → True

By definition of the doubling time under $y=y_0 e^{kt}$.

$$y(T_{\times 2})=y_0 e^{k\cdot(\ln 2)/k}=2y_0$$

The level is exactly double at that clock.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

Write $\ln y(t)=\ln y_0+kt$.

The slope in the $(t,\ln y)$-plane is exactly $k$.

Semi-log slope recovers the same force.

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Rebuilt force $k=\ln(y_1/y_0)/t_1\approx0.03$. Doubling $\approx23.1049$, tripling $\approx36.6204$. Semi-log slope equals $k$.

tasks.title: Applied letters — GDP per capita force via logs
tasks.context: Aggregate GDP and population follow $Y(t)=Y_0 e^{gt}$ and $N(t)=N_0 e^{pt}$ with $Y_0=100$, $g=0.03$, $N_0=10$, $p=0.01$. Per capita is $y=Y/N$. Horizon $t=20$. The figure tracks both scales. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The change in log GDP per capita over $20$ years equals $(g-p)t$.
Log aggregate GDP rises by less than $0.5$ over the $20$-year horizon.
The per-capita force is strictly larger than $0.025$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Logs turn the quotient into a difference of forces.

$$\ln y(t)=\ln(Y_0/N_0)+(g-p)t$$

$$\Delta\ln y=(g-p)t=0.4$$

The log-per-capita change is exactly $(g-p)t$.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Compare with $0.5$.

$$\Delta\ln y=0.4\le 0.5$$

The log change is $0.4$, not above $0.5$.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

Per capita is a ratio, so forces subtract.

$$k_y=g-p=0.02\neq g+p=0.04$$

Adding forces would track $Y\cdot N$, not $Y/N$.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → False

Aggregate log-growth is $gt$.

$$\Delta\ln Y=gt=0.6$$

$$0.6\not< 0.5$$

Log GDP rises by $0.6$, which is not less than $0.5$.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → False

Compare $k=g-p$ with $0.025$.

$$k=0.02\le 0.025$$

The per-capita force equals $0.02$.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Per-capita force $k=g-p=0.02$. Over $t=20$, $\Delta\ln y=0.4$, $\Delta\ln Y=0.6$, $\Delta\ln N=0.2$.

tasks.title: Hybrid — continuous versus discrete log hitting times
tasks.context: A balance starts at $P=1000$. Compare continuous force $k=0.05$ with discrete annual base $a=1.04$ when chasing target $M=2000$. The figure overlays both compounding conventions. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The continuous model reaches the target strictly sooner than the discrete model.
The one-year continuous multiplier $e^{0.05}$ differs from the discrete base $1.04$.
Both models share the same hitting time for the target.
The continuous hitting time is strictly less than $20$ years.
The discrete model reaches the target strictly sooner than the continuous model.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Solve both hitting clocks with logarithms.

$$t_c=\frac{\ln(M/P)}{k}\approx13.8629$$

$$t_d=\frac{\ln(M/P)}{\ln a}\approx17.673$$

$$13.8629<17.673$$

Continuous compounding wins the race to the target.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Compare one-year multipliers.

$$e^{0.05}\approx1.051271,\qquad a=1.04$$

The multipliers differ, so the paths are not reparametrisations.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → False

The two hitting times computed above are unequal.

$$13.8629\neq17.673$$

Shared hitting time fails.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$t_c\approx13.8629<20$$

Continuous hitting finishes inside twenty years.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → False

The inequality runs the other way.

$$t_d\approx17.673>t_c$$

Discrete compounding is slower to the target.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Continuous hit $t_c=\ln(2)/k\approx13.8629$; discrete hit $t_d=\ln 2/\ln a\approx17.673$. $e^{k}\approx1.051271\neq a=1.04$.

tasks.title: Graph — radioactive half-lives beside an investment hitting clock
tasks.context: A sample of $m_0=80$ grams has half-life $T_{1/2}=8$ hours. Separately, an investment of $P=5000$ compounds continuously at force $r=0.05$ toward goal $7000$. The figure overlays both clocks. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: After three half-lives the sample has mass strictly below $15$ grams.
The investment reaches $7000$ in strictly less than $10$ years.
The decay constant equals the investment force $r=0.05$.
Three half-lives span strictly more calendar time than the investment needs to hit its goal.
Substituting the investment hitting time recovers the goal balance.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Three half-lives leave one eighth of the mass.

$$m(3T_{1/2})=80/8=10$$

$$10<15$$

Remaining mass is $10$ grams.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Solve $P e^{rt}=\mathrm{goal}$.

$$t_{\mathrm{goal}}=\frac{\ln(7000/5000)}{r}\approx6.7294$$

$$6.7294<10$$

The investment clock finishes inside ten years.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → False

$$k_{\mathrm{dec}}\approx0.086643\neq r=0.05$$

Decay force and investment force are different parameters.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$3T_{1/2}=24,\qquad t_{\mathrm{goal}}\approx6.7294$$

$$24>6.7294$$

Three half-lives take longer than the investment hit.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

By construction of the continuous hitting time,

$$P e^{r t_{\mathrm{goal}}}=goal=7000$$

Substitution recovers the goal exactly.

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Decay $k_{\mathrm{dec}}=\ln 2/8\approx0.086643$; after $3T_{1/2}=24$ mass is $10$. Investment hits $7000$ at $t\approx6.7294$.

tasks.title: Table — elasticity schedule beside an exponential stock
tasks.context: Demand follows $\ln Q=a-b\ln P$ while a separate stock follows $N(t)=N_0 e^{kt}$. Parameters are tabulated. Horizon $t=10$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: At the stated price, quantity is strictly less than $5$.
At $t=10$ the growing stock exceeds $1.4$ times its initial level.
The demand elasticity equals the stock's continuous force $0.04$.
The stock force recovered from $\ln(N(10)/N_0)/10$ differs from $0.04$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$|\varepsilon|=b=1.4>1$$

Demand is elastic, not inelastic.

So the statement is False.

**B.** → False

$$Q=e^{a-b\ln P}\approx31.8789$$

$$31.8789\not< 5$$

Quantity is far above $5$.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → True

$$N(10)=N_0 e^{kt}\approx298.3649$$

$$1.4 N_0=280$$

The stock clears the $1.4$ threshold.

So the statement is True.

**D.** → False

Elasticity $b$ and force $k$ live in different models.

$$b=1.4\neq k=0.04$$

Equating elasticity with the stock force is a category error.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → False

$$\frac{1}{t}\ln\frac{N(t)}{N_0}=k=0.04$$

Log recovery returns exactly $k$, so they do not differ.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Demand $\ln Q=5-1.4\ln P$ at $P=3$ gives $Q\approx31.8789$ with $|\varepsilon|=1.4$. Stock $N(10)\approx298.3649$.

tasks.title: Symbolic — change-of-base logarithm inside a power equation
tasks.context: Relate powers of $8$ and $2$ through $\log_{2}(8)$. Solve $8^1.6666666666666667=2^{5}$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: That solution is strictly larger than $5$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$\log_{2}(8)=\frac{\ln 8}{\ln 2}=3$$

The logarithm is the integer $3$.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Take $\log_{2}$ of both sides of $8^1.6666666666666667=2^{5}$.

$$x\log_{2}(8)=5$$

$$x=\frac{5}{\log_{2}(8)}=1.666667$$

Change-of-base produces that exact quotient.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → False

$$x=1.666667<5$$

The solution is smaller than the exponent, not larger.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → False

$$a^{x}=b^{5}=32,\qquad b^{5+1}=64$$

Substitution recovers $b^{5}$, not $b^{6}$.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → False

$$\log_{2}(8)=3\le 4$$

The logarithm equals $3$, not above $4$.

So the statement is False.

tasks.title: Parametric — force family pinned by a log constraint
tasks.context: Consider the family $P_\lambda(t)=A e^{\lambda t}$ with fixed $A=100$ and force parameter $\lambda>0$. A distinguished member $\lambda^*$ satisfies $\ln\lambda^*=-\ln 5$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Every force $\lambda>\lambda^*$ has a strictly shorter doubling time than $\lambda^*$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$\ln\lambda^*=-\ln 5\implies\lambda^*=e^{-\ln 5}=\frac{1}{5}$$

The log constraint pins $\lambda^*=1/5$.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

$$P_{\lambda^*}(\ln 5)=A\exp\bigl(\tfrac15\ln 5\bigr)=A\cdot 5^{1/5}>A$$

A positive exponent lifts the level above $A$.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

$$t_{\times 2}=\frac{\ln 2}{\lambda^*}=5\ln 2$$

Doubling time is exactly $5\ln 2$.

So the statement is True.

**D.** → True

$$\ln P_\lambda(t)=\ln A+\lambda t$$

$$\frac{\partial}{\partial\lambda}\ln P_\lambda(t)=t$$

The cross-partial in force is calendar time.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

Doubling time $t_{{\times 2}}=\ln 2/\lambda$ is strictly decreasing in $\lambda>0$.

Any larger force doubles strictly sooner.

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Constraint $\ln\lambda^*=-\ln 5$ pins $\lambda^*=1/5$. Doubling $t_{\times 2}=5\ln 2\approx3.4657$. Larger $\lambda$ shortens doubling.

tasks.title: Piecewise — GDP force switch read through per-capita logs
tasks.context: Aggregate GDP grows at force $g=0.03$ until $t=5$ and at force $k_2=0.015$ afterward. Population grows steadily at force $p=0.01$. Initial per capita is $y_0=Y_0/N_0=50$. Horizon $t=15$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: At $t=15$, GDP per capita exceeds $1.1$ times its initial level.
After the switch, the per-capita force equals $0.015+0.01$.
After the switch, the per-capita force equals $0.015-0.01$.
Keeping the early GDP force all the way to $t=15$ mis-states the true per-capita level.
At the switch time, per capita already exceeds its initial level.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$y(15)\approx58.0917,\qquad 1.1 y_0=55$$

Per capita clears the $1.1$ threshold.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Per capita is a ratio, so forces subtract.

$$k_y=k_2-p=0.005\neq k_2+p=0.025$$

Adding forces would track $Y\cdot N$.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → True

$$k_y=0.015-0.01=0.005$$

The late per-capita force is the difference.

So the statement is True.

**D.** → True

$$y_{\mathrm{wrong}}\approx67.4929\neq y(15)\approx58.0917$$

Ignoring the GDP switch mis-states the terminal level.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

$$y(T)\approx55.2585>y_0=50$$

Early force $g-p>0$ already lifts per capita by the kink.

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Per-capita force is $0.02$ then $0.005$. $y(T)\approx55.2585$, $y(15)\approx58.0917$. Ignoring the switch gives $67.4929$.

tasks.title: Nested — log-pinned force and its inverse clock
tasks.context: A normalised stock $f(t)=e^{kt}$ ($f(0)=1$) has force $k>0$ fixed by $\ln k=-1$. Let $g$ be the inverse of $f$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The number $0$ lies in the domain of $g$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$\ln k=-1\implies k=e^{-1}$$

The nested (here single) log pins the force.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → False

$$g(e)=\frac{\ln e}{k}=\frac{1}{k}=e$$

$$e\neq e^{-1}$$

The inverse clock returns $e$, not $e^{-1}$.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → True

$$g(1)=\frac{\ln 1}{k}=0$$

The inverse of the initial level is time zero.

So the statement is True.

**D.** → False

Range of $f$ is $(0,\infty)$, which excludes $0$.

Zero is not in the domain of $g$.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → True

$$g(e^{k})=\frac{\ln(e^{k})}{k}=\frac{k}{k}=1$$

One year of force maps back to calendar time $1$.

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Force constraint $\ln k=-1$ gives $k=e^{-1}$. Inverse $g(y)=\ln y/k$ sends $1\mapsto 0$ and $e^{k}\mapsto 1$, while $g(e)=e$.

tasks.title: Text-dense — half-life force tangled with an EAR claim
tasks.context: A sample decays with half-life $T_{1/2}=10$. Separately a loan quotes nominal annual rate $r=0.06$ compounded $n=12$ times per year. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The continuous decay constant equals $0.1$ exactly.
The effective annual rate of the loan strictly exceeds the nominal rate $r$.
Using the loan force $r$ as if it were a decay constant would give half-life $\ln 2/r\approx11.5525$. That equals $T_{1/2}$.
The continuous-equivalent annual yield $e^{r}-1$ equals the loan's EAR.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$k=\frac{\ln 2}{10}\approx0.069315\neq 0.1$$

Half-life $10$ does not produce force $0.1$.

So the statement is False.

**B.** → True

$$\mathrm{EAR}=\bigl(1+\frac{r}{n}\bigr)^12.0-1\approx0.061678$$

$$0.061678>0.06$$

Intra-year compounding lifts EAR above the nominal.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → False

$$\ln(1+\mathrm{EAR})\approx0.05985\neq r=0.06$$

That log recovers the continuous force equivalent to EAR, not $r$.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → False

$$\frac{\ln 2}{r}\approx11.5525\neq T_{1/2}=10$$

Loan force and decay half-life are unrelated.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → False

$$e^{r}-1\approx0.061837,\qquad \mathrm{EAR}\approx0.061678$$

Continuous yield on $r$ is not the discrete EAR.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Decay $k=\ln 2/10\approx0.069315$. Nominal $r=0.06$ with $n=12$ gives EAR $\approx0.061678$.

tasks.title: Rebuild — semi-log table forces and equal-ratio check
tasks.context: A continuous exponential stock is sampled at three times (table). The figure shows the semi-log path. Rebuild the force from the outer samples. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The semi-log slope between $t=0$ and $t=8$ equals the continuous force $k=0.045$.
The discrete model $y(t)=P_0(1+0.045)^{t}$ matches the continuous path for all $t$.
Doubling time is strictly less than $10$ years.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$\frac{\ln y(8)-\ln y(0)}{8}\approx0.045$$

Outer semi-log slope recovers $k$.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → False

$$P_0=y(0)=500\neq 600$$

The initial level is $500$, not $600$.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

$$1+k=1.045,\qquad e^{k}\approx1.046028$$

Discrete base $1+k$ is not the continuous multiplier $e^{k}$.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → False

$$t_{\times 2}=\frac{\ln 2}{k}\approx15.4033$$

$$15.4033\not< 10$$

Doubling takes about $15.4$ years.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → True

Equal time steps on a pure exponential give equal ratios.

$$\frac{y(4)}{y(0)}=e^{4k}=\frac{y(8)}{y(4)}\approx1.1972$$

The two successive ratios match.

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Semi-log slope $\approx0.045$ recovers $k=0.045$. Equal time steps give equal ratios $y_{t+\Delta}/y_t=e^{k\Delta}\approx1.1972$.

tasks.title: Applied letters — two funds, log crossing, and who leads after
tasks.context: Fund $A$ follows $A(t)=A_0 e^{\alpha t}$ and fund $B$ follows $B(t)=B_0 e^{\beta t}$ with $A_0=800$, $\alpha=0.04$, $B_0=1200$, $\beta=0.02$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: That meeting time is strictly positive.
For every $t>t^{*}$, fund $A$ strictly exceeds fund $B$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Set $A_0 e^{\alpha t}=B_0 e^{\beta t}$ and take logs.

$$t^{*}=\frac{\ln(B_0/A_0)}{\alpha-\beta}$$

The log crossing formula matches the claim.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

$$t^{*}\approx20.2733>0$$

Because $B_0>A_0$ and $\alpha>\beta$, the crossing is in the future.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

After the crossing the higher force dominates.

$$\alpha-\beta=0.02>0$$

so $A(t)/B(t)$ is strictly increasing through $1$ at $t^{*}$.

Fund $A$ leads for all later times.

So the statement is True.

**D.** → True

$$\ln\frac{A(t)}{B(t)}=\ln\frac{A_0}{B_0}+(\alpha-\beta)t$$

Log-quotient is affine in $t$ with slope $\alpha-\beta$.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

$$B_0=1200>A_0=800$$

Initially $B$ is larger.

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Funds $A(t)=800e^{0.04t}$, $B(t)=1200e^{0.02t}$. Crossing $t^*=\ln(B/A)/(\alpha-\beta)\approx20.2733$; thereafter $A$ leads because $\alpha>\beta$.

tasks.title: Hybrid — piecewise stock force beside constant-elasticity demand
tasks.context: A stock starts at $P_0=1000$, grows at force $k_1=0.05$ until $t=4$, then at force $k_2=0.02$. Separately prices drift at force $g=0.03$ with demand elasticity magnitude $b=1.5$. Read the stock at horizon $t=10$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The average stock force $\bar k=\ln(f(10)/P_0)/10$ exceeds $0.03$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$f(t)=P_0 e^{k_1 T}e^{k_2(t-T)}$$

$$\ln(f(t)/P_0)=k_1 T+k_2(t-T)=0.32$$

Logs add across the kink.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

$$\bar k\approx0.032>0.03$$

Path-average force clears $0.03$.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

$$\frac{d\ln Q}{dt}=-bg=-0.045$$

Constant elasticity converts price force into quantity force.

So the statement is True.

**D.** → False

$$b=1.5>1$$

Demand is elastic.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → True

$$f(t)=P_0 e^{\bar k t}\approx1377.1278$$

$$1.3 P_0=1300$$

The stock clears the $1.3$ threshold.

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Piecewise log-increment $k_1 T+k_2(t-T)=0.32$, $\bar k\approx0.032$. Quantity force $-bg=-0.045$.

tasks.title: Graph — semi-log straightness and three tempting misreads
tasks.context: A level $y(t)=P_0 e^{kt}$ with $P_0=2000$ and $k=0.02$ is plotted on a semi-log chart (figure): vertical axis $\ln y$, horizontal axis $t$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The semi-log graph is a straight line.
The slope of that line equals $P_0=2000$.
The vertical intercept of $\ln y$ equals $P_0$.
The discrete path $P_0(1+0.02)^{t}$ shares the same semi-log slope $k$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$\ln y(t)=\ln P_0+kt$$

An affine function of $t$ is a straight semi-log graph.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → False

$$\mathrm{slope}=k=0.02\neq P_0$$

Slope is the force, not the initial level.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

$$\ln y(0)=\ln P_0\approx7.6009\neq P_0$$

The intercept is $\ln P_0$, not $P_0$.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → False

$$y(\ln 2/k)=P_0 e^{\ln 2}=2P_0\neq 4P_0$$

That clock is doubling, not quadrupling.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → False

$$\ln\bigl(P_0(1+k)^{t}\bigr)=\ln P_0+t\ln(1+k)$$

$$\ln(1+k)\approx0.019803\neq k$$

Discrete semi-log slope is $\ln(1+k)$, not $k$.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: $\ln y(t)=\ln P_0+kt$ with $P_0=2000$, $k=0.02$ is affine; slope $k$, intercept $\ln P_0\approx7.6009$.

tasks.title: Table — continuous versus annual balances and log returns
tasks.context: Principal $P=1000$ at nominal rate $r=0.05$. The table compares continuous $A_c=Pe^{rt}$ with annual $A_d=P(1+r)^10.0$. The figure overlays both. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: At $t=10$, continuous compounding exceeds annual compounding.
The average continuous force implied by $A_d$, namely $\ln(A_d/P)/10$, is strictly less than $r$.
The continuous model reaches the annual model's $10$-year balance in strictly less than $10$ years.
The continuous balance exceeds the annual balance (strict inequality of levels).
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$A_c\approx1648.72>A_d\approx1628.89$$

Continuous wins at the shared horizon.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

$$\ln(A_c/P)=\ln(e^{rt})=rt$$

Log-return of continuous compounding is exactly $rt$.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

$$\frac{\ln(A_d/P)}{t}=\ln(1+r)\approx0.04879<0.05$$

Strict concavity of $\ln$ forces $\ln(1+r)<r$.

So the statement is True.

**D.** → True

$$t^*=\frac{\ln(A_d/P)}{r}\approx9.758<10$$

Continuous compounding hits the annual terminal early.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

$$A_c-A_d\approx19.83>0$$

Levels differ strictly.

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: At $t=10$: $A_c\approx1648.72$, $A_d\approx1628.89$. Continuous time to match $A_d$ is $t^*\approx9.758$. Average discrete force $\ln(1+r)\approx0.04879$.

tasks.title: Symbolic — which exp/log identities survive beside growth
tasks.context: Let $k$ be a real force and $t$ a real time. Let $u,v>0$ be positive levels. Judge each identity claim on its own. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Natural log undoes the exponential.

$$\ln(e^{kt})=kt$$

This is the defining inverse identity.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

$$e^{\ln u}=u\qquad(u>0)$$

Exponential undoes the natural log on $(0,\infty)$.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

$$\ln(uv)=\ln u+\ln v$$

Log turns products into sums.

So the statement is True.

**D.** → False

Counter-example: $u=v=e$ gives $\ln(2e)=\ln 2+1$ while $\ln u+\ln v=2$.

$$\ln 2+1\neq 2$$

Logs do not linearise sums.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → False

$$(e^{k})^{t}=e^{kt}\neq e^{k+t}$$

Exponents multiply under powering, they do not add that way.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Standard identities: $\ln(e^{kt})=kt$, $e^{\ln u}=u$ ($u>0$), $\ln(uv)=\ln u+\ln v$. Sums and the false exponent rule break.

tasks.title: Parametric — log domain side-conditions on an exponential stock
tasks.context: A stock $N(t)=A e^{kt}$ carries auxiliary log expressions $\ln(A-1)$ and $\ln(2-k)$ that must be defined in the reals. Suppose the calibrated pair is $A=e$ and $k=\dfrac{1}{2}$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The expression $\ln(2-k)$ requires $k>2$ as a domain condition.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$A=e>1$$

The level clears the domain threshold for $\ln(A-1)$.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

$$k=\tfrac12<2$$

The force sits below the domain threshold for $\ln(2-k)$.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → False

$$\ln(A-1)=\ln(e-1)\neq 0$$

$e-1\neq 1$, so the log is not zero.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → False

Natural log $\ln(2-k)$ needs $2-k>0$, i.e. $k<2$.

The domain inequality runs $k<2$, not $k>2$.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → False

$$N(0)=A=e\neq 1$$

Initial stock equals $A=e$, not $1$.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Side-conditions $\ln(A-1)$ and $\ln(2-k)$ force $A>1$ and $k<2$. Here $A=e$ and $k=0.5$ obey both; $\ln(A-1)=\ln(e-1)\neq 0$.

tasks.title: Piecewise — true log-average versus arithmetic mean of forces
tasks.context: A fund starts at $P_0=900$, grows at force $k_1=0.07$ until $t=2$, then at force $k_2=0.03$ through horizon $t=8$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The late force is strictly larger than the early force.
At $t=8$ the fund lies strictly below $P_0$.
Doubling time from $P_0$ equals $\ln 2/k_1$ even after the switch.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$\ln(f(t)/P_0)=k_1 T+k_2(t-T)=0.32$$

Logs add across segments.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → False

$$\bar k=\frac{k_1 T+k_2(t-T)}{t}=0.04\neq0.05$$

Time-weighted average is not the arithmetic mean of the two forces.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

$$k_2=0.03<k_1=0.07$$

The late force is smaller.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → False

$$f(t)\approx1239.415>P_0$$

Positive forces lift the fund above $P_0$.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → False

After the switch the correct doubling solve uses both segments.

$$\frac{\ln 2}{k_1}\approx9.9021$$

is only valid if $2P_0$ is reached before the kink — not guaranteed as a general rule.

The constant-$k_1$ doubling clock ignores the switch.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: True average $\bar k=0.04$ from weighted forces; naive $(k_1+k_2)/2=0.05$ differs. $f(8)\approx1239.415$.

tasks.title: Nested — double-log constraints pinning level and force
tasks.context: A normalised stock $N(t)=e^{kt}$ is aimed at a level $A>e$. The pair $(A,k)$ satisfies $\ln(\ln A)=\ln 2$ and $\ln(\ln(1/k))=0$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The hitting time of level $A$ equals $2e$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$\ln(\ln A)=\ln 2\implies\ln A=2\implies A=e^{2}$$

Unwinding both logs pins $A=e^{2}$.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

$$\ln(\ln(1/k))=0\implies\ln(1/k)=1\implies 1/k=e\implies k=e^{-1}$$

The nested constraint on $1/k$ pins the force.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

$$t=\frac{\ln A}{k}=\frac{2}{e^{-1}}=2e$$

Hitting time is exactly $2e$.

So the statement is True.

**D.** → True

This is the given constraint, already verified by $A=e^{2}$.

$$\ln(\ln e^{2})=\ln 2$$

The outer nested log recovers $\ln 2$.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

$$Ak=e^{2}\cdot e^{-1}=e$$

The product collapses to $e$.

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Nested constraints give $A=e^2$, $k=e^{-1}$. Hitting $A$ from $N(0)=1$ takes $t=\ln A/k=2e\approx5.4366$.

tasks.title: Text-dense — inverse clock traps beside exponential growth
tasks.context: Let $f(t)=P e^{kt}$ with $P=50$ and $k=0.1$, and let $g$ be its inverse. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: $g(-1)$ is defined as a real number.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$g(2P)=\frac{1}{k}\ln 2=\frac{\ln 2}{0.1}$$

Doubling the level takes time $\ln 2/k$.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

$$g(P)=\frac{1}{k}\ln 1=0$$

The inverse of the initial level is time zero.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → False

Range of $f$ is $(0,\infty)$; $-1$ is outside.

$g(-1)$ is not real-defined.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → False

Right-inverse identity needs $y>0$.

$y=-3$ is not in the range of $f$.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → False

$$g(f(3))=3$$

$$3\neq\frac{1}{0.1}$$

Left inverse returns the original time $3$.

So the statement is False.

tasks.title: Rebuild — two series, two forces, one future crossing
tasks.context: Two continuous exponential series $A$ and $B$ are each observed at two times (table). Rebuild both forces, then locate their crossing. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The implied meeting time is strictly positive.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$k_A=\frac{\ln(A(5)/A(0))}{5}=0.03$$

Log recovery returns force $0.03$.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

$$k_B=\frac{\ln(B(5)/B(0))}{5}=0.01$$

Log recovery returns force $0.01$.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

$$t^*=\frac{\ln(B_0/A_0)}{k_A-k_B}\approx20.2733>0$$

A future crossing exists.

So the statement is True.

**D.** → False

$$t^*\approx20.2733>5$$

The crossing lies after the observation window.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → False

$$A(5)\approx1161.83,\qquad B(5)\approx1576.91$$

At the second observation $B$ is still larger.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Rebuilt $k_A\approx0.03$, $k_B\approx0.01$. Meeting $t^*\approx20.2733$ lies after the observation window.

tasks.title: Applied letters — nested log link between GDP and population forces
tasks.context: GDP and population forces $g$ and $p$ satisfy the nested-log link $\ln(g/p)=\ln 3$, with $p=0.01$. Horizon $t=25$, initial levels $Y_0=120$, $N_0=8$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Over the horizon, $\Delta\ln y$ strictly exceeds $\Delta\ln N$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$\ln(g/p)=\ln 3\implies g/p=3\implies g=3p$$

The nested log link collapses to $g=3p$.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

$$k=g-p=0.03-0.01=0.02$$

Per-capita force is the difference.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

$$\Delta\ln y=kt=0.5$$

Log per-capita change is force times horizon.

So the statement is True.

**D.** → True

$$\Delta\ln y=0.5,\qquad \Delta\ln N=pt=0.25$$

$$0.5>0.25$$

Per-capita log-growth outpaces population log-growth.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$g+p=0.04\neq k=0.02$$

Sums of forces do not give per-capita force.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Constraint $\ln(g/p)=\ln 3$ forces $g=3p$. With $p=0.01$, $g=0.03$, $k=g-p=0.02$, $\Delta\ln y=0.5$ over $t=25$.
